NgZ7N1W5ulQ.one_line: Between rakaat on the 28th night: those saved on the Day of Judgement look for their brothers, so the congregation pledges to take each other's hand.
NgZ7N1W5ulQ.summary: On the twenty-eighth night of Ramadan 2026 the single reminder between rakaat builds to a shared act the congregation is meant to remember. Starting from a verse recited that night in Az-Zumar, that Allah will save the God-conscious and grant them success, he turns to salvation on the Day of Judgement: after crossing the bridge over Hell there comes a moment on the far side when a person knows he is saved. That is the deep reason it is recommended to get to know as many believers as possible: once across, you look around for the people you knew and ask where they are. At the arched bridge before Paradise and in the places where Allah permits intercession, believers plead for their brothers and sisters, and that, he says, is what brotherhood means. He then asks everyone to take the hands of the people on their right and left and make a covenant that whoever among them is saved will take his brother's or sister's hand on that Day, reminding them that Allah commands fulfilling covenants, and closes asking Allah to save them all from the Fire.

uBpazmjT1kc.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Workshop on Similar Verses (Adh-Dhariyat and Al-Ma'arij)
uBpazmjT1kc.one_line: A group exercise comparing two similar passages: the muhsinin of Adh-Dhariyat who go beyond, and the musallin of Al-Ma'arij who keep the minimum.
uBpazmjT1kc.summary: The speaker shows that clusters of verses that sound alike, which reciters often confuse, are never random. He gives four tools for comparing them: context before and after, keywords, subtle differences in wording and word order, and the occasion of revelation, noting that Arabic fronts what matters most, as in 'You alone we worship'. Groups then compare Adh-Dhariyat 51:15-19 with Al-Ma'arij 70:19-35. In Adh-Dhariyat the muhsinin, people who go the extra mile, sleep little at night, seek forgiveness before dawn, and give the asker and the deprived an unspecified right in their wealth. In Al-Ma'arij the anxious, grasping human is excepted only if he is one of the musallin, a noun describing people whose identity is prayer: they keep it constantly, recognise a known right of others in their wealth, believe in the Day of Judgment, are deeply concerned about their Lord's punishment, guard their chastity, keep trusts and covenants, uphold testimony and protect their prayers. He concludes that Al-Ma'arij sets the floor no believer may fall below, while Adh-Dhariyat describes a higher rank of voluntary excellence, and urges reading the Quran slowly with attention to such differences.

outline.heading: Similar clusters at the end of the Quran
outline.gist: Some passages share wording and even verse length but are not identical; the exercise is to find out why.

outline.heading: Interlude

outline.gist: Reciters confuse such passages; first assume a reason and read what comes before and after.

outline.heading: Keywords and subtle differences
outline.gist: Each cluster has a keyword that Allah builds on, and the wording differs in small, meaningful ways.

outline.heading: The keyword of each passage
outline.gist: One passage builds on the muhsinin, the other on the human being and his description.

outline.heading: Occasion of revelation and word order
outline.gist: Arabic fronts what is most important, as in 'You alone we worship' rather than 'we worship You'.

outline.heading: Interlude
They slept little of the night
outline.gist: Fronting 'little' emphasizes how little they slept, spending the night in prayer and dua.

outline.heading: Seeking forgiveness before dawn
outline.gist: The same fronting highlights that the pre-dawn hours are given to istighfar.

outline.heading: A right, but not a known right
outline.gist: Adh-Dhariyat says 'a right' for the asker and the deprived, while Al-Ma'arij says 'a known right': voluntary giving versus the fixed obligation.

outline.heading: Muhsinin: those who go the extra mile
outline.gist: Ihsan always describes doing more than required, such as staying up at night and giving without counting.

outline.heading: Read slowly and look before and after
outline.gist: Reciting is not enough; contemplate the verse, the page before and the page after.

outline.heading: The anxious human being
outline.gist: The insan is never praised in the Quran: impatient, despairing in hardship and withholding in ease.

outline.heading: Except the musallin: prayer as identity
outline.gist: The noun musallin, rather than 'those who pray', describes people so constant in prayer that it defines them.

outline.heading: Constant in their prayer
outline.gist: Their day is scheduled around the prayer times.

outline.heading: A known right in their wealth
outline.gist: Part of every income belongs to someone else; the sunnah fixes it at two and a half percent for the asker and the deprived.

outline.heading: Interlude
From outward practice to inner belief
outline.gist: These verses set the bare minimum; after the physical practices come what they believe.

outline.heading: Believing in the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: Belief in accountability is what keeps a person from despair in hardship and stinginess in ease.

outline.heading: Concerned about their Lord's punishment
outline.gist: Mushfiqun means ongoing concern, which differs from simple fear.

outline.heading: Guarding chastity
outline.gist: No relationships outside what Islam permits; those who seek beyond it are transgressors who cross the line.

outline.heading: Keeping trusts and covenants
outline.gist: The amanah the heavens and mountains declined includes every covenant with Allah and every trust between people.

outline.heading: None of these may be broken
outline.gist: Unlike night prayer, these qualities are not optional; truthful testimony is among them.

outline.heading: Beginning and ending with prayer
outline.gist: The passage opens with constancy in prayer and closes with guarding it, and its people are honoured in gardens.

outline.heading: Which group ranks higher?
outline.gist: The muhsinin go above and beyond and rank higher; the musallin describe the floor no believer can go below.

outline.heading: Another similar cluster and repeated stories
outline.gist: The opening of Al-Mu'minun sounds similar again; repeated stories such as Nuh and Adam are each worded differently for a reason.

outline.heading: Interlude
Question: is the fuller description lower?
outline.gist: A questioner notes Al-Ma'arij lists more qualities; he answers that its items are obligatory, while the muhsinin give without limit.

outline.heading: Outro

My Lord hath made it true, and He hath shown me kindness, since He took me out of the prison and hath brought you from the desert after Satan had made strife between me and my brethren. Lo! my Lord is tender unto whom He will. He is the Knower, the Wise

66:8.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوۡبَةࣰ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَيُدۡخِلَكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ يَوۡمَ لَا يُخۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥۖ نُورُهُمۡ يَسۡعَىٰ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتۡمِمۡ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
66:8.en: O ye who believe! Turn unto Allah in sincere repentance! It may be that your Lord will remit from you your evil deeds and bring you into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, on the day when Allah will not abase the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands; they will say: Our Lord! Perfect our light for us, and forgive us! Lo! Thou art Able to do all things

42:25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
42:25.en: And He it is Who accepteth repentance from His bondmen, and pardoneth the evil deeds, and knoweth what ye do

25:68.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامࣰ ا
25:68.en: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty

25:69.ar: يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25:69.en: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

1hBPaO-AKfI.speaker: guest
1hBPaO-AKfI.speaker_note: a different speaker delivers a structured, student-style talk in mixed Arabic and English; the title names no speaker and the delivery is not the sheikh's
1hBPaO-AKfI.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Tawbah and Forgiveness
1hBPaO-AKfI.one_line: Using the last nights to seek forgiveness: Allah's names of forgiveness, forgiving others like Abu Bakr and Yusuf, and the conditions of sincere tawbah.
1hBPaO-AKfI.summary: The speaker starts from Ramadan being a counted number of days that pass quickly, like life itself, and the story of two companions where the one who lived a year longer, fasting and praying more, entered paradise first. The last nights are like a treasure room open for thirty minutes, and forgiveness is its greatest treasure, since the one who reaches Ramadan unforgiven is warned and Laylat al-Qadr can equal a lifetime. He distinguishes istighfar from tawbah: major or repeated sins need regret and a plan to change. He explains Al-Ghafur and Al-Ghaffar, from a root meaning to cover, and Allah's concealment of our sins; every human errs, and the best are those who keep returning, as a child gets back on the bike. The Quran tells us to walk for provision but to race toward forgiveness and flee to Allah. Forgiving others is a path to being forgiven, as with Abu Bakr and Mistah and Yusuf, who forgave his brothers without reminding them. Tawbah is returning to the path like a rerouting map, and its conditions are stopping the sin, regret, resolving not to return, and repairing harm, after which Allah turns bad deeds into good.

outline.heading: Opening
A counted number of days
outline.gist: Ramadan passes as quickly as life does; with three nights left, ask whether you used the time well.

outline.heading: The companion who lived one more year
outline.gist: Of two men who accepted Islam together, the one who outlived the martyr by a year entered paradise first, because of the extra Ramadan and prayers.

outline.heading: A treasure room open for thirty minutes
outline.gist: Would you spend limited access to a room of treasure scrolling Instagram, or seek the most valuable thing in it?

outline.heading: Forgiveness, the greatest treasure
outline.gist: The Prophet said ameen on the minbar to Jibril's dua against one who reaches Ramadan and is not forgiven.

outline.heading: Laylat al-Qadr: one moment worth a lifetime
outline.gist: A single act of high-quality worship can earn the reward of a thousand months; this may be our last chance.

outline.heading: Istighfar versus tawbah
outline.gist: For major or repeated sins asking forgiveness is not enough; one must regret the sin and plan to rectify it.

outline.heading: Maghfirah means covering
outline.gist: The root of Allah's names of forgiveness means to cover; His concealment of our sins is a mercy, or we could not face one another.

outline.heading: Al-Ghafur and Al-Ghaffar
outline.gist: Al-Ghafur forgives every kind of sin, great and small; Al-Ghaffar, in an intensive form, keeps forgiving time after time.

outline.heading: Every human errs; get back on the bike
outline.gist: The best sinners are those who repent; like a child who falls off a bike, we keep returning to Allah, who forgives sins that reach the sky.

outline.heading: Everything forgiven except shirk
outline.gist: Allah forgives all sins below associating partners with Him for whom He wills.

outline.heading: Walk for provision, race for forgiveness
outline.gist: The Quran says to walk the earth for provision but to hasten and compete for forgiveness.

outline.heading: Remember Allah and flee to Him
outline.gist: Those who wrong themselves remember Allah and seek forgiveness; the believer flees back to Him.

outline.heading: Forgive to be forgiven: Abu Bakr and Mistah
outline.gist: After the slander against Aisha, Abu Bakr swore to stop supporting Mistah, and was told: do you not love that Allah forgive you?

outline.heading: Yusuf forgives his brothers
outline.gist: Thrown in a well, enslaved and imprisoned, Yusuf told his brothers there is no blame today and later mentioned only the prison, blaming Shaytan for the rift.

outline.heading: Forgiveness without reminding
outline.gist: Real forgiveness does not keep count, humiliate or remind the person; ask who in your life you can forgive.

outline.heading: Tawbah means returning to the route
outline.gist: Sincere repentance is like a map app rerouting you to the original path after a wrong turn; At-Tawwab keeps accepting the return.

outline.heading: A clean slate
outline.gist: Allah accepts repentance from His servants and pardons their bad deeds.

outline.heading: Come walking and He comes running
outline.gist: In a hadith qudsi, whoever meets Allah with an earth-full of sins, without shirk, is met with as much forgiveness.

outline.heading: First condition: stop the sin
outline.gist: You cannot claim to return to Allah while still committing the sin.

outline.heading: Second condition: genuine regret
outline.gist: Without believing the act is wrong, as with someone who does not think smoking is haram, behaviour never changes.

outline.heading: Third condition: a plan not to return
outline.gist: Identify what pulls you back, such as friends or environment, and plan how to leave it.

outline.heading: Fourth condition: repair the harm
outline.gist: Those who repent, believe and do righteous deeds have their bad deeds replaced with good ones.

outline.heading: Transformed in the last nights
outline.gist: He asks that we leave Ramadan forgiven, transformed and connected to the Quran.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Tawbah is returning to the path; for major or repeated sins it requires stopping, regret, a plan and repairing harm.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Ghafur, Al-Ghaffar and At-Tawwab describe a Lord who covers sins and keeps forgiving.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgiving others, without reminding or humiliating them, is a way to earn Allah's forgiveness.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The last nights are a limited treasure room whose greatest prize is forgiveness.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: One extra year of fasting and prayer raised a companion above a martyr; time slips by like Ramadan.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Yusuf's forgiveness of his brothers is the model of forgiving without reproach.

quran.point: Fasting is for a counted number of days.
Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.
By time, mankind is in loss.
Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives anything less for whom He wills.
After prayer disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty.
Walk through the earth and eat of His provision: walking for rizq.
Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord.
Race toward forgiveness from your Lord.
Those who commit an indecency or wrong themselves remember Allah and seek forgiveness.
So flee to Allah.
Let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah forgive you?
No blame on you today.
Yusuf mentions being freed from prison and blames Shaytan for the rift, not his brothers.
Turn to Allah in sincere repentance.
He accepts repentance from His servants and pardons bad deeds.
Except whoever repents, believes and does righteous deeds: Allah replaces their bad deeds with good.

hadith.gist: Talhah dreamt that of two companions, the one who died a year after the martyr entered paradise first; the Prophet explained he had fasted another Ramadan and prayed so many more prayers.
The Prophet said ameen on the minbar when Jibril prayed against the one who reaches Ramadan and is not forgiven.
Allah looked at the people of Badr and said do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.
Every child of Adam errs, and the best of those who err are those who repent.
O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me I will forgive you, even if your sins reach the clouds of the sky.
Whoever comes to Allah walking, He comes to him running; whoever meets Him with an earth-full of sins without shirk, He meets with as much forgiveness.

maxims: Walk for provision, race for forgiveness
Forgiveness that comes with counting is not forgiveness

stories.who: Two companions, one martyred and one who lived a year longer
stories.point: An extra Ramadan of fasting and prayer can outweigh martyrdom; value the time left.

stories.who: Abu Bakr and Mistah after the slander of Aisha
stories.point: Forgiving those who wronged you is how you seek Allah's forgiveness.

stories.who: Yusuf and his brothers
stories.point: True forgiveness never reminds or humiliates the one forgiven.

takeaways: Treat the remaining nights as limited access to a treasure and seek forgiveness above all.
For repeated or major sins, stop, regret, plan to avoid the triggers, and repair any harm done.
Forgive someone who wronged you, and do not remind them of it afterwards.
Keep returning to Allah after every fall instead of giving up.

2:183.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:183.en: O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)

2:197.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرࣱ مَّعۡلُومَٰتࣱۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
2:197.en: The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months, and whoever is minded to perform the pilgrimage therein (let him remember that) there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage. And whatsoever good ye do Allah knoweth it. So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil. Therefore keep your duty unto Me, O men of understanding

7:26.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ قَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ لِبَاسࣰ ا يُوَٰرِي سَوۡءَٰتِكُمۡ وَرِيشࣰ اۖ وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
7:26.en: O Children of Adam! We have revealed unto you raiment to conceal your shame, and splendid vesture, but the raiment of restraint from evil, that is best. This is of the revelations of Allah, that they may remember

9:109.ar: أَفَمَنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ تَقۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنٍ خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارࣲ فَٱنۡهَارَ بِهِۦ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
9:109.en: Is he who founded his building upon duty to Allah and His good pleasure better; or he who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling, overhanging precipice so that it toppled with him into the fire of hell? Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

65:2.ar: فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفࣲ وَأَشۡهِدُواْ ذَوَيۡ عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجࣰ ا
65:2.en: Then, when they have reached their term, take them back in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men among you, and keep your testimony upright for Allah. Whoso believeth in Allah and the Last Day is exhorted to act thus. And whosoever keepeth his duty to Allah, Allah will appoint a way out for him

65:3.ar: وَيَرۡزُقۡهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَحۡتَسِبُۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمۡرِهِۦۚ قَدۡ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدۡرࣰ ا
65:3.en: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things

66:6.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيكُمۡ نَارࣰ ا وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلۡحِجَارَةُ عَلَيۡهَا مَلَٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظࣱ شِدَادࣱ لَّا يَعۡصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمۡ وَيَفۡعَلُونَ مَا يُؤۡمَرُونَ
66:6.en: O ye who believe! Ward off from yourselves and your families a Fire whereof the fuel is men and stones, over which are set angels strong, severe, who resist not Allah in that which He commandeth them, but do that which they are commanded

50:19.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنۡهُ تَحِيدُ
50:19.en: And the agony of death cometh in truth. (And it is said unto him): This is that which thou wast wont to shun

3:185.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
3:185.en: Every soul will taste of death. And ye will be paid on the Day of Resurrection only that which ye have fairly earned. Whoso is removed from the Fire and is made to enter paradise, he indeed is triumphant. The life of this world is but comfort of illusion

21:34.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا لِبَشَرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ ٱلۡخُلۡدَۖ أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِدُونَ
21:34.en: We appointed immortality for no mortal before thee. What! if thou diest, can they be immortal

21:35.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَنَبۡلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلۡخَيۡرِ فِتۡنَةࣰۖ وَإِلَيۡنَا تُرۡجَعُونَ
21:35.en: Every soul must taste of death, and We try you with evil and with good, for ordeal. And unto Us ye will be returned

39:30.en: Lo! thou wilt die, and lo! they will die

4:78.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُرُوجࣲ مُّشَيَّدَةࣲۗ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِكَۚ قُلۡ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفۡقَهُونَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:78.en: Wheresoever ye may be, death will overtake you, even though ye were in lofty towers. Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah; and if an evil thing befalleth them they say: This is of thy doing (O Muhammad). Say (unto them): All is from Allah. What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening

23:99.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ
23:99.en: Until, when death cometh unto one of them, he saith: My Lord! Send me back

23:100.ar: لَعَلِّيٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُۚ كَلَّآۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَاۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
23:100.en: That I may do right in that which I have left behind! But nay! It is but a word that he speaketh; and behind them is a barrier until the day when they are raised

39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
39:67.en: And they esteem not Allah as He hath the right to be esteemed, when the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are rolled in His right hand. Glorified is He and High Exalted from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

39:68.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۖ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخۡرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ قِيَامࣱ يَنظُرُونَ
39:68.en: And the trumpet is blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are in the earth swoon away, save him whom Allah willeth. Then it is blown a second time, and behold them standing waiting

22:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡۚ إِنَّ زَلۡزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَيۡءٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
22:1.en: O mankind! Fear your Lord. Lo! the earthquake of the Hour (of Doom) is a tremendous thing

22:2.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَوۡنَهَا تَذۡهَلُ كُلُّ مُرۡضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرۡضَعَتۡ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمۡلٍ حَمۡلَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَٰرَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَٰرَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّ عَذَابَ ٱللَّهِ شَدِيدࣱ‏
22:2.en: On the day when ye behold it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling and every pregnant one will be delivered of her burden, and thou (Muhammad) wilt see mankind as drunken, yet they will not be drunken, but the Doom of Allah will be strong (upon them)

53:58.ar: لَيۡسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
53:58.en: None beside Allah can disclose it

53:59.en: Marvel ye then at this statement

50:41.ar: وَٱسۡتَمِعۡ يَوۡمَ يُنَادِ ٱلۡمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانࣲ قَرِيبࣲ‏
50:41.en: And listen on the day when the crier crieth from a near place

50:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يَسۡمَعُونَ ٱلصَّيۡحَةَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلۡخُرُوجِ
50:42.en: The day when they will hear the (Awful) Cry in truth. That is the day of coming forth (from the graves)

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day

20:105.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡجِبَالِ فَقُلۡ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسۡفࣰ ا
20:105.en: They will ask thee of the mountains (on that day). Say: My Lord will break them into scattered dust

20:106.en: And leave it as an empty plain

20:107.ar: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجࣰ ا وَلَآ أَمۡتࣰ ا
20:107.en: Wherein thou seest neither curve nor ruggedness

23:112.ar: قَٰلَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ
23:112.en: He will say: How long tarried ye in the earth, counting by years

23:113.ar: قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲ فَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡعَآدِّينَ
23:113.en: They will say: We tarried by a day or part of a day. Ask of those who keep count

23:114.ar: قَٰلَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ لَّوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
23:114.en: He will say: Ye tarried but a little if ye only knew

40:16.ar: يَوۡمَ هُم بَٰرِزُونَۖ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِنۡهُمۡ شَيۡءࣱۚ لِّمَنِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
40:16.en: The day when they come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. Whose is the Sovereignty this day? It is Allah's, the One, the Almighty

18:100.en: On that day we shall present hell to the disbelievers, plain to view

18:101.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَانَتۡ أَعۡيُنُهُمۡ فِي غِطَآءٍ عَن ذِكۡرِي وَكَانُواْ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ سَمۡعًا
18:101.en: Those whose eyes were hoodwinked from My reminder, and who could not bear to hear

89:23.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
89:23.en: And hell is brought near that day; on that day man will remember, but how will the remembrance (then avail him)

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

25:12.ar: إِذَا رَأَتۡهُم مِّن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدࣲ سَمِعُواْ لَهَا تَغَيُّظࣰ ا وَزَفِيرࣰ ا
25:12.en: When it seeth them from afar, they hear the crackling and the roar thereof

77:32.en: Lo! it throweth up sparks like the castles

45:28.ar: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةࣲ جَاثِيَةࣰۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةࣲ تُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:28.en: And thou wilt see each nation crouching, each nation summoned to its record. (And it will be said unto them): This day ye are requited what ye used to do

23:107.ar: رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡهَا فَإِنۡ عُدۡنَا فَإِنَّا ظَٰلِمُونَ
23:107.en: Our Lord! Oh, bring us forth from hence! If we return (to evil) then indeed we shall be wrong-doers

18:49.ar: وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةࣰ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَىٰهَاۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرࣰ اۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:49.en: And the Book is placed, and thou seest the guilty fearful of that which is therein, and they say: What kind of a Book is this that leaveth not a small thing nor a great thing but hath counted it! And they find all that they did confronting them, and thy Lord wrongeth no-one

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

84:10.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ
84:10.en: But whoso is given his account behind his back

89:22.ar: وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفࣰّ ا صَفࣰّ ا
89:22.en: And thy Lord shall come with angels, rank on rank

69:17.ar: وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآئِهَاۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ ثَمَٰنِيَةࣱ‏
69:17.en: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them

68:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقࣲ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
68:42.en: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able

68:43.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
68:43.en: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt

19:71.ar: وَإِن مِّنكُمۡ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَاۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتۡمࣰ ا مَّقۡضِيࣰّ ا
19:71.en: There is not one of you but shall approach it. That is a fixed ordinance of thy Lord

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

pvIzOXvSCUU.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Operationalizing Taqwa and a Tawahhum Exercise
pvIzOXvSCUU.one_line: A practical definition of taqwa applied to money, time and family, followed by a guided contemplation from the deathbed to the final verdict.
pvIzOXvSCUU.summary: The night has two parts. First, in conversation with a guest physician, he treats taqwa as the goal of fasting and asks how to make it measurable. Taqwa is the baseline, not the summit: asking whether something will displease Allah, or whether you will regret it, and braking when the answer is yes, like steering around slush or a car's lane assist. It can only be measured in oneself, and Ramadan removes the usual excuses. The Quran attaches taqwa to the hardest situations, such as fasting and divorce, as a safety valve, and prevention always beats seeking forgiveness afterwards. They apply it to zakat season (riba, shady investments, unpaid debts, withheld inheritance, complicit employers), to time and screen use, where the sheikh notes an hour a day adds up to years, to social media algorithms, and to the home, where family members know a person's real taqwa. Second, the sheikh leads a tawahhum exercise of guided reflection: the angel of death, the departing soul, the grave and its doors, the two blasts of the horn, resurrection, the gathering in sweat, the seven shaded by the Throne, Jahannam paraded, the books, the prostration, the Prophet's basin, the bridge, and standing before Allah for the verdict, with la ilaha illa Allah as the refrain. He asks people to repeat this reflection for a few minutes daily.

outline.heading: Opening
Why do we fast? To gain taqwa
outline.gist: The guest asks the audience why we fast and lands on the verse: fasting was prescribed so that we may attain taqwa.

outline.heading: Operationalizing taqwa: each Ramadan better than the last
outline.gist: The guest says an objective must be made measurable; the test is whether each Ramadan starts higher than the last, so the last is the best.

outline.heading: Defining taqwa: the thorny path
outline.gist: Taqwa is usually defined with words as vague as itself; a companion asked for its meaning answered with a question about walking a path full of thorns.

outline.heading: The Eid sneakers in the slush
outline.gist: The guest updates the image: walking to Eid prayer in prized new shoes, you step around every puddle.

outline.heading: Taqwa as lane assist
outline.gist: Taqwa nudges you back when you drift across Allah's limits; push hard enough and desire overrides it.

outline.heading: Taqwa is the baseline, not the summit
outline.gist: Defining it in lofty terms makes people give up; taqwa is practical and is the minimum standard.

outline.heading: Two questions: will it please or displease Allah?
outline.gist: Asking whether every act pleases Allah is the level of the elite; taqwa only asks whether it displeases Him, then hits the brakes.

outline.heading: The permissible gray zone and preventive character
outline.gist: Most of life is mubah and allowed; taqwa means protection, like preventive medicine for the soul.

outline.heading: Pilgrims who set out without provisions
outline.gist: People of Yemen went to hajj taking nothing, saying Allah will feed us, and died on the way; the Quran told them to take provision, for the best provision is taqwa.

outline.heading: Ask before every step: will I regret this?
outline.gist: Slowing down to ask whether you will regret something here or before Allah is taqwa made operational; aim higher later.

outline.heading: No taqwa meters: flip the camera to yourself
outline.gist: The guest says taqwa was meant as a front-facing camera for self-assessment, but people turned it on everyone else, even children judging others in salah.

outline.heading: Ramadan as the ultimate spiritual selfie
outline.gist: With shaytan chained and everyone on best behaviour, Ramadan removes the excuses, so it is the month to assess yourself.

outline.heading: Taqwa across the Quran
outline.gist: The root appears around 256 times, as the outcome of worship, as a command and as a condition for achievement.

outline.heading: Taqwa as food, clothing and shelter
outline.gist: Allah describes it as provision, as a garment and as a foundation for a building; missing its meaning means missing much of the Quran.

outline.heading: Compare these days to your normal days
outline.gist: Less distraction, less social media, more good deeds: Ramadan shows how much better life is with taqwa.

outline.heading: Taqwa attached to the hardest acts: fasting
outline.gist: Hajj is hard for a few days, but fasting brings weeks of anxiety beforehand, which is why taqwa is tied to it.

outline.heading: Divorce and the page with the most taqwa
outline.gist: Divorce is the hardest social situation, and the opening of At-Talaq mentions taqwa more than any page because that is when you need it most.

outline.heading: Taqwa as the safety valve
outline.gist: When you have lost yourself you can always fall back on one simple question and step away.

outline.heading: You can only measure your own
outline.gist: Count how many decisions today you slowed down for and whether you chose well; judging others' taqwa is none of your business.

outline.heading: Prevention beats damage control
outline.gist: Avoiding the wrong is better ten times out of ten than seeking forgiveness and fatwas afterwards; youth who learn this get far ahead.

outline.heading: Deflection in hard conversations
outline.gist: The guest notes most marital arguments involve justifying or deflecting, the same reflex we use to avoid self-assessment.

outline.heading: 'Worry about yourself': the worst reply
outline.gist: The guest cites the hadith that the worst speech is answering 'fear Allah' with 'mind yourself'.

outline.heading: Three areas to apply taqwa
outline.gist: The guest proposes family relationships, finances and provision as areas to operationalize taqwa.

outline.heading: Provision: where we show the least taqwa
outline.gist: Because income feels vital, people take riba, gray investments, tax shortcuts and benefit claims; Allah promises provision from unexpected places to the mindful.

outline.heading: A way out of financial strain
outline.gist: The promise comes in At-Talaq because divorce causes itemized financial strain, much like the Western context.

outline.heading: Zakat season: audit your wealth
outline.gist: Having just reviewed accounts for zakat, check whether investments are Sharia compliant, whether you owe unpaid debts, and whether a sister's inheritance was withheld.

outline.heading: Zakat is not a blanket purifier
outline.gist: Paying two and a half percent does not clean whatever shady dealings the rest of the wealth carries.

outline.heading: Is your employer a bank or complicit in war?
outline.gist: The guest asks people to consider whether their workplace deals in riba or supports the war on fellow Muslims; Allah promises a better way out.

outline.heading: For the young, taqwa shows in time
outline.gist: Taqwa matters most in the capital you have most of, and for young people that is time.

outline.heading: Reading out your screen time
outline.gist: He polls the room on the weekly phone usage report, as he does in his mentorship program, and finds few under several hours a day.

outline.heading: An hour a day is two years by sixty
outline.gist: Six or eight hours a day would add up to a decade staring at a phone, even granting work and Quran use.

outline.heading: Build on Ramadan's better distribution
outline.gist: Even if total screen time held steady, more of it went to Quran; carry that forward.

outline.heading: One device for guidance and for everything else
outline.gist: The guest asks how the same vessel used to read the Quran can carry everything else.

outline.heading: The attention economy
outline.gist: Platforms keep you scrolling to sell ads and push constant upward comparisons about homes, skin, bodies, cars and spouses.

outline.heading: Train your algorithm
outline.gist: The guest says the algorithm mirrors your lowest self; use Ramadan's taqwa to reshape it, since music and worse slip in through every reel.

outline.heading: Numbing is not self-care
outline.gist: Scrolling gets rebranded as self-care; mark content not interested, block and unfollow.

outline.heading: Haram but make it Muslim
outline.gist: Muslim influencer content often trades on attraction and showing off spouses, accepted because of a beard or hijab.

outline.heading: Retrain it on Mondays and Thursdays
outline.gist: An incognito feed shows how platforms bait attention; voluntary fasts are a good time to clean the feed again.

outline.heading: Your family holds your taqwa meter
outline.gist: The guest says people may smile in the masjid and scowl at home; family members see what you watch and how you behave.

outline.heading: Taqwa starts at home
outline.gist: Protect yourselves and your families; the shepherd is responsible, and the best of people are the best to their families.

outline.heading: Interlude
An exercise of reflection, not an act of worship
outline.gist: The tawahhum exercise needs complete silence; it is contemplation, not a sunnah ritual, though contemplation is central to the deen.

outline.heading: Walking through the stations of the hereafter
outline.gist: He narrates the Quran- and sunnah-based journey after death station by station, with ten tahlils between stations, while listeners imagine themselves at its centre.

outline.heading: Practise it a few minutes daily
outline.gist: Reflecting on verses about death and judgment has a profound effect on behaviour, closeness to Allah and taqwa.

outline.heading: Interlude
The angel of death arrives
outline.gist: A creature no one else sees sits at your head with companions in white or otherwise; you cannot speak and the stupor of death comes with truth.

outline.heading: Remembering your choices
outline.gist: Lying there you recall your regrets and the people you wronged, gripped by sadness or calm depending on your direction.

outline.heading: Every soul shall taste death
outline.gist: Verses on death's certainty: no one was granted immortality, the Prophet too would die, and death finds you even in fortified towers.

outline.heading: Calm soul or wicked soul
outline.gist: The angel addresses you by your name and your father's name, calling the soul out to Allah's mercy or to His wrath.

outline.heading: The spirit leaves the body
outline.gist: Numbness rises from the feet, regrets flood in, and all you can hope for is that your tongue says la ilaha illa Allah.

outline.heading: 'Send me back' and the barzakh
outline.gist: The dying beg to return and do good; the answer is no, and a barrier stands until resurrection.

outline.heading: How the soul departs
outline.gist: A good soul slips out like a drop from a spout, a bad one like a dry branch pulled from damp wool, and is wrapped in a shroud from paradise or the Fire.

outline.heading: The grave and the soul's ascent
outline.gist: The grave is the first station: if you pass it what follows is easier; the soul is carried up, the heavens open or stay shut, and it is praised or scorned.

outline.heading: Truly alone for the first time
outline.gist: Even the womb had warmth; the grave is tight and dark, and doors open onto paradise and onto Jahannam.

outline.heading: One door closes forever
outline.gist: You spend your time in the grave looking through the door that stays open, either longing for the Hour or dreading it.

outline.heading: Your deeds keep you company; the three questions
outline.gist: Prayer, zakat and fasting sit around you to shield you, and you are asked about your Lord, your Prophet and your religion.

outline.heading: Only one phrase saves you in the grave
outline.gist: Whatever you prepared, the testimony of faith is what rescues you there.

outline.heading: The first blast of the horn
outline.gist: Humanity, still arguing and debating, waits for a single blast from the angel created for it.

outline.heading: It comes without warning
outline.gist: A man repairing an appliance, another lifting food to his mouth, two people haggling over a garment: none finish.

outline.heading: The earth folded in His hand
outline.gist: They did not revere Allah as He deserves; the earth and heavens are in His grip, and the blast ends all life, even in the graves.

outline.heading: The last angels die
outline.gist: The angel of death takes the hornblower, then Jibril, then his own soul, until no one remains.

outline.heading: 'I am the King: where are the kings?'
outline.gist: Allah alone, as He always was, calls into the void asking where the kings and tyrants of the earth are.

outline.heading: The second blast: resurrection
outline.gist: Life rushes into everything that ever lived and your consciousness returns in the grave.

outline.heading: The quake of the Hour
outline.gist: Nursing mothers forget their infants, pregnancies end, and people look drunk from fear.

outline.heading: The approaching Hour and the caller
outline.gist: Do you laugh rather than weep at this news? Everyone answers the caller who calls from a near place.

outline.heading: Your body recreated
outline.gist: After ages in the earth your veins, nerves and skin are rebuilt exactly as you remember, and you brush off the dust.

outline.heading: Fleeing familiar faces
outline.gist: You see siblings, parents, children and friends, and people run so their eyes do not fall on faces that remind them of their wrongs.

outline.heading: Locusts in every direction, families holding hands
outline.gist: Most run in fear toward the caller, but some families stand together calmly, strengthening one another.

outline.heading: The universe crumbles
outline.gist: The sun is rolled up, stars fall, and mountains are marched off and blown into dust.

outline.heading: Witnessing what you always knew
outline.gist: Everything Allah described is now in front of you, and the only true word left is the testimony of faith.

outline.heading: The flat white land of judgment
outline.gist: No hills, valleys, rocks or shade, nowhere to hide and nothing to put between you and others.

outline.heading: Unclothed and searching for cover
outline.gist: You suddenly notice you are naked, as is everyone, and all you want is something to cover yourself.

outline.heading: Coverings of different lengths
outline.gist: Some trail long garments, some barely cover themselves, and whether your faults are covered depends on your choices.

outline.heading: How people arrive at the gathering
outline.gist: Some ride, some walk, some are dragged on their faces, some are tiny as ants, some sit on pedestals of light with loved ones.

outline.heading: How long did you stay on earth?
outline.gist: They say a day or part of a day, and are told they lived only a little, if only they had known.

outline.heading: The sun brought near and the sea of sweat
outline.gist: Sweat rises to ankles, waists or mouths according to deeds, and people search for relief.

outline.heading: Shade of the Throne, by invitation only
outline.gist: A shade appears on the horizon, but humanity is stopped and names are called.

outline.heading: First of the seven: just leaders
outline.gist: Just rulers are called into the shade.

outline.heading: Second of the seven: youth raised in worship
outline.gist: Young people who spent their best years serving Allah are called.

outline.heading: Third of the seven: hearts attached to the masjid
outline.gist: Those who cannot wait to return to the masjid are called.

outline.heading: Fourth of the seven: love for Allah's sake
outline.gist: Pairs who met and parted for Allah walk toward the shade.

outline.heading: Fifth of the seven: resisting temptation
outline.gist: Those offered haram who refused are called, and very few move.

outline.heading: Sixth of the seven: secret charity
outline.gist: Those whose left hand did not know what the right gave are called.

outline.heading: Seventh of the seven: tears in private
outline.gist: Those who remembered Allah alone and wept are called, and each group leaves chanting the testimony of joy. Are you still standing in the sweat?

outline.heading: The rumbling and the call of sovereignty
outline.gist: The earth shakes, nothing is hidden, and the call rings out: to whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Jahannam paraded before the disbelievers
outline.gist: It is displayed to those whose eyes were veiled from remembrance; people remember everything, too late.

outline.heading: Taken before the judgment begins
outline.gist: Some are plucked from the crowd into the Fire before any reckoning, and you ask what they did.

outline.heading: First thrown: the reciter
outline.gist: He claims he recited for Allah and is told he recited to be called a reciter.

outline.heading: Second thrown: the scholar
outline.gist: He learned so people would call him a scholar, and they did.

outline.heading: Third thrown: the martyr
outline.gist: He fought to be called brave, and he was.

outline.heading: Fourth thrown: the philanthropist
outline.gist: He gave to be called generous among his peers, and he was.

outline.heading: Ransoming with one's own family
outline.gist: Seeing Jahannam, people offer their children, spouses, siblings, kin and everyone on earth in their place.

outline.heading: The fury of Jahannam
outline.gist: Its roar is heard from afar, sparks fly like castles, and it is held by seventy thousand reins, each with seventy thousand angels.

outline.heading: Knees that buckle
outline.gist: Everyone falls to their knees, glancing sideways at a fire kindled for thousands of years until it turned black.

outline.heading: 'Our Lord, bring us out'
outline.gist: From inside comes the plea to be returned to do right, and everyone watching can only say la ilaha illa Allah.

outline.heading: The books fly to their owners
outline.gist: Like a thousand arrows on the horizon, every record heads to its owner, and the guilty despair at its detail.

outline.heading: Read your book
outline.gist: Nothing small or great is left out, your Lord wrongs no one, and you are told to be your own accountant.

outline.heading: Right hand, left hand or behind the back
outline.gist: Those who know their book will come in the left hand hide it behind them, and it lands there anyway.

outline.heading: Your Lord comes with the angels
outline.gist: Rows of angels fill every corner, and eight mighty angels carry the Throne.

outline.heading: The call to prostrate
outline.gist: Some fall into sujud in honour; others find their backs rigid as metal because they refused to prostrate in life, and no one can help them.

outline.heading: Interlude
The basin seen from afar
outline.gist: Thirsty and exhausted, you approach a crowd gathered around a great basin of water purer than silver.

outline.heading: The Prophet at his basin
outline.gist: It smells better than musk, is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey, with cups like stars, and the man you heard of all your life stands there.

outline.heading: Seeing his face for the first time
outline.gist: You push through the crowd toward the most beautiful smile you have ever seen as he fills cup after cup.

outline.heading: Turned away from the basin
outline.gist: An angel blocks a man from the cup; the Prophet pleads that he is of his ummah and is told he does not know what they changed after him.

outline.heading: Your turn at the basin
outline.gist: He promised to meet you at the basin; you extend your hand hoping no barrier comes between you and the cup.

outline.heading: The cliff of Jahannam and the bridge
outline.gist: Everyone comes to a cliff so deep a stone falls for seventy years, with a path across it finer than a hair.

outline.heading: Crossing like lightning, wind or step by step
outline.gist: People cross at the speed of their deeds, as they walked the path of the deen in this life.

outline.heading: The light you carry
outline.gist: Hypocrites beg the believers to wait so they can borrow light and are told to go back and seek it; a wall comes between them.

outline.heading: Hooks along the bridge
outline.gist: Hooks snatch at people in proportion to what they took in this world; some freeze, some crawl, and one drops just before reaching the far side.

outline.heading: The Prophet's intercession and the hundred mercies
outline.gist: He prostrates beneath the Throne asking mercy for his ummah, and Allah joins the one mercy He sent to earth with His ninety-nine.

outline.heading: Reading your book before the scales
outline.gist: The reckoning begins, and the more you read, the more you wish things were not there.

outline.heading: Waiting for your name
outline.gist: You watch others celebrated or dragged away until you are called to stand in the court where only justice is served.

outline.heading: Standing before Allah
outline.gist: Reading your book aloud, you hope to rush past what shames you; if fortunate He accepts your apology quickly.

outline.heading: Awaiting the verdict
outline.gist: No earlier pain or joy compares to the word that decides the rest of your existence.

outline.heading: The only word with the weight to save you
outline.gist: The angels tell you that la ilaha illa Allah alone carries the weight to save you that day.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Taqwa is the baseline question of whether an act displeases Allah or will be regretted, applied as a brake before acting.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Taqwa can only be measured in oneself; turning it on others and deflecting criticism are the common failures.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Divorce is the hardest social situation, which is why At-Talaq repeats taqwa so often.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Provision is where people show the least taqwa: riba, gray investments, unpaid debts, withheld inheritance and complicit employers.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: The zakat audit is a chance to examine all of one's wealth, not a blanket purification of it.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: For the young, time is the capital where taqwa shows; an hour a day becomes years of a life.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: Screen time, the attention economy and algorithms that mirror the lowest self; retrain the feed as you train the nafs.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Family members see a person's real taqwa; it starts at home with protecting oneself and one's family.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Contemplation is a central but neglected practice; a few minutes a day of reflecting on death changes behaviour.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The horn, resurrection, the gathering, the shade, Jahannam, the books, the basin, the bridge and the verdict, with the testimony of faith as the only rescue.

Take provision for hajj, and the best provision is taqwa.
The garment of taqwa is the best garment.
A building founded on taqwa: taqwa as shelter.
Whoever has taqwa, Allah makes a way out for him and provides from where he does not expect.
Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire.
The stupor of death comes with the truth: what you were avoiding.
Every soul shall taste death.
No human before you was granted immortality; if you die, will they live forever?
You will die and they will die.
Death will reach you even in lofty towers.
The dying beg to be sent back; behind them is a barrier until resurrection.
They did not revere Allah as He deserves; the earth in His grip and the blast of the horn.
The quake of the Hour makes nursing mothers forget their infants.
The approaching Hour has drawn near; do you laugh and not weep?
The caller calls from a near place and all hear the blast in truth.
They come out like scattered locusts, rushing toward the caller.
The sun is wrapped up and the stars fall.
Allah will blast the mountains to dust and leave a level plain with no crookedness.
How long did you remain on earth? A day or part of a day.
To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.
Jahannam is displayed to those whose eyes were veiled from remembrance.
On that day man will remember, but what use is remembering then?
The criminal would ransom himself with his children, spouse, brother, kin and everyone on earth.
When it sees them from afar they hear its fury and roaring.
It throws sparks as huge as castles.
Every nation will be seen kneeling.
Our Lord, bring us out; if we return we would be wrongdoers.
What is this book that leaves nothing small or great unrecorded? Your Lord wrongs no one.
Read your book; you suffice today as your own accountant.
Whoever is given his book behind his back.
Your Lord comes with the angels rank upon rank.
Eight angels carry the Throne of your Lord that day.

hadith.gist: A companion asked about taqwa replied by asking whether he had walked a thorny path and how he gathered himself to avoid the thorns.
The worst speech is when a man is told 'fear Allah' and replies 'mind yourself'.
The best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family.

The angel of death sits at the head of the dying and calls the good soul out to Allah's forgiveness and pleasure and the wicked soul to His wrath; the good soul flows out like a drop from a waterskin, the other is dragged like a skewer through wet wool.
The grave is the first station of the hereafter; whoever is saved from it finds what follows easier.
In the grave prayer stands at the head, zakat at the right and fasting at the left to shield the believer.
The Hour will come while two men have spread a garment between them and not finished their sale, and a man raises food to his mouth and does not eat it.
Allah will fold the heavens and the earth and say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?
On the Day of Resurrection people will be in sweat according to their deeds, to their ankles, knees, waists or mouths.

Seven are shaded by Allah on the day there is no shade but His: the just ruler, the youth raised in worship, the one attached to the masjid, two who love for Allah, the one who refuses temptation, the secret giver and the one who weeps remembering Allah alone.
The first judged and thrown into the Fire are a reciter, a scholar, a martyr and a generous man who acted to be praised.
Jahannam is brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
The Fire was kindled a thousand years until red, a thousand until white and a thousand until black.
The Prophet's basin is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey with cups as many as the stars; some will be driven away and he will be told he does not know what they changed after him.
On the bridge people pass like lightning, wind and swift horses, with hooks that snatch them.
Allah has a hundred mercies; He sent one to earth and kept ninety-nine for the Day of Resurrection.

ZA7FIIfzn24.speaker: adnan
ZA7FIIfzn24.speaker_note: continues his own values series and speaks of his personal struggle with forgiveness
ZA7FIIfzn24.title: The Values of Islam: Forgiveness and Pardoning (Maghfirah and 'Afw)
ZA7FIIfzn24.one_line: Forgiveness and pardoning are high ideals built on justice; on the 27th night, forgive others as you hope Allah forgives you.
ZA7FIIfzn24.summary: On the eve of the 27th night of Ramadan he turns to forgiveness and pardoning as they come from people, not from Allah. These are high-order ideals that the earlier ethics exist to protect: one cannot preach forgiveness where rights are violated, just as outward sunnah means nothing alongside eating haram. He lists the scholars' conditions for forgiveness: it must be for Allah, the wronged person must be capable of reclaiming the right, and it must lead to reconciliation rather than encouraging the wrongdoer. Asking the oppressed to forgive while their right is still held is shameful; forgiving what you cannot reclaim is weakness. Forgiveness means not seeking accountability and unloading a burden the wrongdoer has long forgotten, though distance may remain; pardoning goes further, restoring the relationship as if nothing happened. He tells of Abu Bakr resuming support of Mistah after the slander of Aishah when the Quran asked whether he did not love Allah's forgiveness, admitting he has not yet managed such forgiveness. He cites Ibrahim and Isa leaving their people to Allah's forgiveness, the Prophet's night spent on one verse, and the dua against grudges. He asks each listener to find someone to forgive tonight, stressing the choice is theirs.

outline.heading: Opening
Forgiving others on the 27th night
outline.gist: To obtain forgiveness on this night one must offer it to others; the talk concerns forgiveness from people, not from Allah.

outline.heading: Ideals that the basic ethics protect
outline.gist: Forgiveness and pardoning are high ideals of elegance that require justice and trustworthiness first; the series was ordered for this reason.

outline.heading: Ideals without foundations
outline.gist: Outward sunnah alongside haram earnings makes no sense; justice must be bolted down before calling the oppressed to forgive.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: for the sake of Allah
outline.gist: Forgiveness is not a transaction or a favour to be returned later.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: capability
outline.gist: One can only forgive a right one is able to reclaim; telling the oppressed to forgive while their right is still taken is shameful.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: no harm
outline.gist: Forgive only when it brings reconciliation, not when it encourages the wrongdoer to keep transgressing.

outline.heading: Reclaim the right first
outline.gist: The Prophet told the companions to go after the wealth taken from them before choosing to forgive, since forgiving what you cannot reach is weakness.

outline.heading: Forgive those who do not hope for Allah's days
outline.gist: The Quran urges forgiving offenders because their reckoning is heavy; forgiveness goes against human nature and takes deliberate effort.

outline.heading: Forgiveness unloads your own burden
outline.gist: The wrongdoer forgets while the wronged carries the bitterness; forgiving cleanses the heart, though trust and distance may remain.

outline.heading: Pardoning restores the glass
outline.gist: 'Afw goes beyond forgiveness, returning the relationship to how it was, as the Prophet was told to pardon and say peace.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr, Aishah and Mistah
outline.gist: The slander devastated Abu Bakr, who swore to cut off support from Mistah, a relative he had been funding.

outline.heading: Do you not love that Allah forgives you?
outline.gist: The verse revealed after the slander moved Abu Bakr to restore Mistah's support for life.

outline.heading: Maybe tonight
outline.gist: He admits he has never managed to imagine forgiving like Abu Bakr and hopes each year this night will be the one.

outline.heading: Forgiveness is true strength and raises rank
outline.gist: Those who persevere and forgive show real resolve, and Allah only increases a servant in honour for pardoning.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and Isa leave their people to Allah
outline.gist: Both prophets entrusted sinners to Allah's forgiveness, and the Prophet spent a whole night reciting Isa's verse.

outline.heading: The Prophet carried no grudges
outline.gist: Pardoning differs from mercy, which is empathy, and from tawbah, which is changing oneself.

outline.heading: A dua against grudges
outline.gist: Later believers asked Allah to forgive those before them and remove any grudge from their hearts.

outline.heading: Most grievances are petty: let them go
outline.gist: Usually you could reclaim your right but it is not worth it, and living with the bitterness wastes your life; still, no one can force you to forgive.

outline.heading: Who do you need to forgive?
outline.gist: He asks each listener to find someone to forgive, especially those who never apologized, promising Allah will give more in return.

outline.heading: Allah loves to pardon
outline.gist: The Prophet's dua for these nights asks the One who loves pardoning; the question is whether we can do it ourselves.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgiveness and pardoning are ideals with conditions, an unburdening of the self and a way to earn Allah's pardon.

QfqJzQzsuNM.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 28 - Quranic Themes: Insights
QfqJzQzsuNM.one_line: Insight as seeing past appearances: man is a witness against himself (75:14-15), every soul knows what it brought (81:14), and bystanders are not innocent (85:7).
QfqJzQzsuNM.summary: He defines insight as seeing what lies beneath surfaces and argues that losing it means losing everything. In an age of cosmetic surgery and AI fakes the eyes are easily fooled, but the heart is not: gut feelings are not proof, yet should never be ignored, and many great scholars were blind yet saw deeply. Insight is strong in youth and either sharpens or dulls with age; without it people choose ruinous spouses or, worst of all, arrive on Judgement Day sure they did well, the greatest losers of 18:103-104. From al-Qiyamah he shows that doubts about resurrection mask a wish to follow desire, while 75:14-15 says every person is a witness to himself despite his excuses. We can fool everyone, even ourselves for a while, but not Allah, just as parents see through a child's lies. At-Takwir's scenes of cosmic collapse end with every soul knowing what it has brought, so he urges people to level with themselves now and ask for mercy like Yusuf's brothers with their poor goods, since no one else really cares. Finally al-Buruj's people of the ditch include those who sat and watched: silence before oppression is a choice that will be answered for.

outline.heading: Sight versus insight
outline.gist: Eyes see packaging and masks; insight sees what is inside and what really happened.

outline.heading: Lose insight and you lose everything
outline.gist: Eyes are fooled by any magician, but looking with the eyes of the heart always finds the way back to what is right.

outline.heading: An age of optical illusions
outline.gist: Cosmetic surgery remakes people and AI will make every photo and video worthless as evidence until verified, yet the heart still senses when something is wrong.

outline.heading: Do not ignore your gut
outline.gist: Intuition is not proof and should not be acted on alone, but it is given for a reason and should be heard and honed.

outline.heading: Blind scholars and blind hearts
outline.gist: Countless scholars were born blind yet had extraordinary insight into revelation and the seerah; it is hearts that go blind, not eyes.

outline.heading: Healthy bodies without insight
outline.gist: Some people lecture on morality with no insight into the state of their own lives and families.

outline.heading: Insight and choosing a spouse
outline.gist: The young see clearly, but insight sharpens or dulls with age; a woman blind to a harmful man or a man losing his family over a bad match shows desire overriding insight.

outline.heading: 18:103-104: the greatest losers
outline.gist: Self-honesty keeps you from drifting unaware; the biggest losers are those who thought they were doing well and arrive expecting approval.

outline.heading: His friend who always aced the exam
outline.gist: A friend left every exam certain he had done well and scored half; over-optimism without honest self-assessment costs dearly.

outline.heading: 75:3-12: the real reason for denial
outline.gist: Man claims Allah cannot reassemble his bones, but the real issue is wanting an excuse to follow desire guilt-free; on that day he will ask where to flee.

outline.heading: 75:14-15: a witness against himself
outline.gist: Whatever excuses he offers, man knows exactly why he did what he did; he can fool spouse, parents and community, even himself, but not Allah.

outline.heading: An inner compass
outline.gist: Imagine not knowing your own motives; Allah gave a compass that always tells you whether you were selfish, petty or sincere.

outline.heading: Admit it to yourself
outline.gist: 75:13 says man will be told all he did, though he does not need telling; you need not confess to others, but you must be honest with yourself.

outline.heading: Children's lies and our excuses to Allah
outline.gist: Parents see straight through a child's lies, and we do the same with Allah; raising children is the closest thing we have to understanding that relationship.

outline.heading: 81:1-4: the cosmos unravels
outline.gist: The sun wound into a ball, stars falling to dust, mountains moved like powder and pregnant animals abandoned.

outline.heading: 81:5: the animals gathered
outline.gist: Every creature is a nation like us and will be brought back, so treat animals as neighbours and partners on earth.

outline.heading: 81:6-7: seas ablaze and souls paired
outline.gist: Oceans catch fire, and each person is joined with those most like them; no one stands alone.

outline.heading: 81:8-11: the buried girl is asked
outline.gist: Murdered children will be asked for what sin they were killed, including babies buried under their bombed homes; records are spread and the sky stripped away.

outline.heading: 81:12-14: every soul knows what it brought
outline.gist: Hell is kindled and Paradise brought near, and every soul knows exactly what it carries.

outline.heading: Level with yourself now
outline.gist: Use the insight you already have to admit who you are without decoration; that honesty is the launching pad for change.

outline.heading: A dua that relies on mercy alone
outline.gist: In the last nights, ask Allah as Yusuf's brothers asked with their worthless goods: we bring little, so be charitable to us.

outline.heading: No one else really cares
outline.gist: The social web of opinions and status means nothing; people will not ask after you, and the only one who has ever truly cared is Allah.

outline.heading: Standing amid it all, knowing
outline.gist: As creation is remade you will know what you brought; leveling with yourself now spares you the greatest disappointment.

outline.heading: Interlude
The people of the ditch
outline.gist: A king burned believers one by one in a fiery trench for refusing to give up their faith, and they stood firm.

outline.heading: Oaths by the witness and the witnessed
outline.gist: Allah swears by the constellations, the promised day and every witness and thing witnessed before cursing the people of the ditch.

outline.heading: Three groups at the trench
outline.gist: The cursed are not only those who dug it; there were the believers, the criminals and a third group who sat and watched.

outline.heading: The silent majority
outline.gist: The neutral onlookers who see and have opinions but say nothing let a harmful minority set the norm; he calls them the biggest evil.

outline.heading: Doing nothing is a choice
outline.gist: The idea that it is not your problem is foreign to Islam; standing by while people are stripped of rights is a decision.

outline.heading: The eldest who 'didn't do anything'
outline.gist: Parents blame the eldest when the younger ones wreck the house; before Allah, having done nothing is exactly the charge.

outline.heading: Witnesses will answer
outline.gist: Those who watched oppression and went to sleep knew what they could have done; you would never accept that excuse if you were the one under fire.

60:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ تُلۡقُونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِمَا جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ يُخۡرِجُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ رَبِّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ خَرَجۡتُمۡ جِهَٰدࣰ ا فِي سَبِيلِي وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِيۚ تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا۠ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَآ أَخۡفَيۡتُمۡ وَمَآ أَعۡلَنتُمۡۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡهُ مِنكُمۡ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
60:1.en: O ye who believe! Choose not My enemy and your enemy for allies. Do ye give them friendship when they disbelieve in that truth which hath come unto you, driving out the messenger and you because ye believe in Allah, your Lord? If ye have come forth to strive in My way and seeking My good pleasure, (show them not friendship). Do ye show friendship unto them in secret, when I am Best Aware of what ye hide and what ye proclaim? And whosoever doeth it among you, he verily hath strayed from the right way

60:7.ar: ۞عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجۡعَلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيۡتُم مِّنۡهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ قَدِيرࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:7.en: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

60:9.ar: إِنَّمَا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخۡرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ وَظَٰهَرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡرَاجِكُمۡ أَن تَوَلَّوۡهُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
60:9.en: Allah forbiddeth you only those who warred against you on account of religion and have driven you out from your homes and helped to drive you out, that ye make friends of them. Whosoever maketh friends of them - (All) such are wrong-doers

64:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡ عَدُوࣰّ ا لَّكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ

64:15.en: Your wealth and your children are only a temptation, whereas Allah! with Him is an immense reward

64:16.ar: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
64:16.en: So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can, and listen, and obey, and spend; that is better for your souls. And whoso is saved from his own greed, such are the successful
